description.value: A cross-sectional study examining the effects of schizophrenia diagnosis and overweight/obesity on gray matter volume using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry, and testing whether bilateral insula gray matter mediates the association between BMI and negative symptoms in schizophrenia.

quotes: The whole-brain voxel-based morphometry was applied to examine the GMV alterations, and a 2 × 2 full factorial analysis of variance was performed to identify the main effects of diagnosis (SZ vs HC), BMI (NW vs OWB) factors, and their interactions.

description.value: Cross-sectional observational study of 250 Chinese Uyghur participants stratified by schizophrenia diagnosis and BMI category; no intervention or longitudinal follow-up was reported.

quotes: This study had a cross-sectional design, which precluded causal inferences, thus longitudinal design is needed to determine whether GMV loss occurred before or after the weight gain abnormalities in patients with SZ.

value: Segmentation into gray matter, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid

quotes: the main steps include: a) discarded the images with visible artifacts; b) format conversion and corrected the image origin (reorientation); c) bias field correction; d) structural images were segmented into three tissue components: gray matter (GM), white matter (WM), and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF); e) the segmented images of all subjects were normalized to the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) space using the DARTEL deformations (resliced into 1.5mm ); f) the resulting GM images ( modulated GMV) were smoothed using an isotropic Gaussian kernel of 8 mm FWHM.
